# Stream-to-Devlog & Trailer Cut Director: Getting Started

Turn recorded gameplay into a devlog or trailer. Choose moments that show the player experience, frame them for each destination and check the cut for sensitive information.

If `engine/lens.mjs`, `engine/lens-kit.mjs` or `fixtures/good-pack.json` are not on disk yet, write them byte for byte from the `trailer-director-lens-engine` skill first (Node 18+, no dependencies).

## 1. Onboard one question at a time

Ask one question at a time, wait for the answer, then ask the next. Never stack questions in one message. Start every profile value from `fixtures/good-pack.json` and ask the owner to confirm or replace it; the sample values are synthetic examples, never defaults.

1. Which game are we working on? Then ask, one at a time: which build should the footage come from (a build id or commit), and what produces the evidence pack (a CI job or a manual capture)?
2. What should a viewer understand or feel by the end of the cut? For example "every level is one screen of tight jumps" or "your farm changes with the seasons".
3. Does your game log its own events, such as level complete, puzzle solved, lap record or story choice? If not, we pick moments by hand while watching.
4. Which formats do you need? Name each cut, for example a wide 16:9 cut for a store page and a vertical 9:16 cut for short-video apps. Add square 1:1 or portrait 4:5 only if you will post to a feed that uses them. Each answer becomes an entry in `deliveryCuts` and one `decodedCuts` case.
5. How long may each cut be on the platforms you chose? This sets `maxLengthS`.
6. How loud should the final mix be, how far off may it be, and how high may its true peak go? This sets `targetLufs`, `lufsTolerance` and `maxTruePeakDb` (in dBTP). Your platforms decide; the sample uses -14, 1 and -1.
7. How far may sound drift from picture before it looks wrong? This sets `maxAvSyncMs`.
8. What share of speech cues must the captions match? This sets `minCaptionMatch`.
9. Which parts of each file should the final review cover? This sets `reviewChannels`: picture, audio, captions, title, filename and metadata.
10. Can the footage show anything private, such as player names, chat, desktop notifications or unreleased content? Who checks it?
11. Who will watch the wide cut and judge whether the action reads? That person records the `readable-story:2` judgement.
12. Who reviews the local finding drafts?

Before grading a real pack, match its build and profile to what the owner approved. Record unavailable capture or execution as NOT_RUN. Run `node engine/lens.mjs --meta` to see the population each line needs (the list or count of things measured, such as shots or caption cues).

## 2. What you provide

- An evidence pack (JSON) with `status: "VALID"`, a `liveSha`, a `gitSha` and a `packId` (all three are required), and an `artifacts` list. Every metric group names the artifact id it came from.
- Metric groups this engine reads: `shots` (capture), `claims` (static), `edl` (static), `cropFraming` (capture), `redaction` (capture), `exports` (capture), `recovery` (capture), `captions` (capture), `sound` (capture), `licensing` (static).
- Profile thresholds in `pack.profile`. A missing threshold makes its line U, never a default.
- Receipts: one result row per test case agreed in `profile.cases`, with the measured values. For example, one `decodedCuts` row per delivery cut with the decoded width, height, frame rate and codec.
- Judgements for the perception lines (`readable-story:2`): `{ level, judge, evidenceIds, note }`, citing artifact ids that exist in the pack.
- Anything you cannot capture yet stays out of the pack. It grades U (UNMEASURED), which is honest and costs no false defect.

## 3. Run the first grade

```
node engine/lens.mjs fixtures/good-pack.json   # worked example, synthetic, not a measurement
node engine/lens.mjs your-pack.json            # your build
node engine/lens.mjs --meta                    # rubric lines, weights and what each reads
node engine/lens.mjs --fixtures fixtures/good-pack.json  # negative and missing-input self-test
```

Read the record: `verdict` (PASS, CONDITIONAL, BLOCKED or INVALID), `grade` and `coverage`, then each line's `level` and `findings`, then `checks` (growth checks reported beside the grade) and `tickets` (deduplicated candidates).

## 4. Report in plain English

- Lead with the verdict, grade and coverage in one sentence. Say how much of the rubric was measured.
- List U lines as "not measured yet" with the capture that would measure them. Never call them defects.
- One local ticket draft per measured finding, with the pack id and artifact ids. Label any synthetic pack as synthetic.
- Rubric lines: authentic-gameplay:1, authentic-gameplay:2, readable-story:1, readable-story:2, composition:1, composition:2, technical-export:1, technical-export:2, accessible-delivery:1, accessible-delivery:2.

## 5. Skills in this template

Use them in this order:

- `gameplay-moment-finder`: picks the moments from the game's own events, the footage or hand picks. Fills `shots`, `claims` and `edl` (authentic-gameplay:1 and 2, readable-story:1).
- `multi-aspect-smart-framing-exporter`: reframes each approved cut, exports it and decodes it. Fills `cropFraming`, `exports`, `recovery` and `licensing` (composition:1, technical-export:1 and 2).
- `beat-sync-and-secret-redaction-gate`: times the cut and reviews every final export. Fills `redaction`, `captions` and `sound` (composition:2, accessible-delivery:1 and 2).
- `trailer-director-lens-engine`: the engine source and how to run it.

## Blockers to tell the owner about

- Action readable in the main wide cut (`readable-story:2`) needs a person to watch the wide cut; it stays U until a named reviewer records a judgement.

Confirm content rights, protected subjects, required formats and the reviewer. For missing footage or tools, draft the outstanding checks locally and record NOT_RUN.

Before capture, agree on the case IDs and expected values in `profile.cases`. Run `node engine/lens.mjs --meta` for the required row fields and comparisons. Record one row per approved case under `receipts`, including its id, liveSha and artifact ID. A skipped or stale case leaves its line U. The bundled rows and budgets are synthetic.

# Find the moments worth cutting

Pick the moments that show what your game is about, from footage of the build you are grading. The game's own events and the footage drive the pick. Loudness, fast motion or a high score never qualify a moment on their own.

## Method
1. Ask the owner, in one sentence, what a viewer should understand by the end of the cut (for example "every level is one screen of tight jumps" or "your farm changes with the seasons").
2. Collect signals from the same build on one timeline:
   - Game events, if your game logs them: level complete, puzzle solved, new area reached, lap record, story choice, item crafted, objective taken.
   - Footage changes: scene cuts, camera moves, on-screen text, music changes, sound onsets.
   - Hand picks: moments the owner or a reviewer marks while watching.
3. Choose the signals that fit your genre and write them, with how much each counts, into the local edit list before ranking. Examples:
   - 2D platformer: a hard jump landed, a secret found, a checkpoint reached.
   - Mobile puzzle game: the last piece settling, a chain reaction, a board cleared.
   - Turn-based strategy game: a flank that turns a battle, a city founded, an end-of-turn reveal.
   - Racing game: an overtake into the last corner, a photo finish, a new lap record.
   - Narrative adventure: a choice and its visible result, a character's first line, a reveal.
   - Farming or life sim: the first harvest, a change of season, a festival, a house upgrade.
   - 3D arena game: a team objective taken, a comeback, a round won. Combat signals belong here, as one genre among many.
4. Hand-picked fallback: when the game logs no events, or none fit (a cozy or puzzle game often has few spikes), watch the footage at playback size and mark moments by hand. Record who picked each one and why. A hand pick is as valid as a logged event.
5. Add lead-in and recovery time so the viewer can follow cause and effect. Drop candidates that tell the same story twice. Trim copies with FFmpeg or your editor and keep the source timecode in the edit list.
6. Review each candidate at its playback size with sound on and off. Save accepted and rejected time ranges with a reason.
7. Check each shot against the build: it comes from the graded build, and no shot or line implies a feature the build does not have.

## What this fills in the pack
- `shots`: total shots, shots from the graded build (`fromGradedBuild`) and shots named in the pack (`namedInPack`).
- `claims`: claims checked (`claimsChecked`) and claims that imply a feature the build lacks (`unavailableImplied`).
- `edl` (the edit decision list): source clips recorded and `decisionsRecorded`, plus one `receipts.editDecisions` row per approved shot.
- `readable-story:2` stays U until a named reviewer watches the wide cut and records a judgement.

## Negative fixture
Add a loud menu transition with no gameplay to the candidates and confirm it is rejected, because volume alone cannot qualify a clip. Add one shot from an older build and confirm `authentic-gameplay:1` drops.

## Worked examples (synthetic)
- Synthetic example, mobile puzzle game: no event log, so the owner marks 14 moments by hand and 6 survive review, all from the graded build. Report: shots 6 of 6 from the graded build, edit list written, readable-story:2 not measured yet.
- Synthetic example, racing game: the event log offers 40 overtakes and 5 are picked; one shows a car that is not in the build. Report: claims checked 9, unavailableImplied 1, top fix: replace that shot.

Tell the owner which lines this moved and which stay unmeasured.

Gather evidence for `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>`.

Push only when the human asks and only to that branch. Never push to main. The human merges and deploys. Any feature switch you add is off by default.

# Reframe and export every delivery cut

Turn one edit into each format the owner approved, keep what matters in frame, then export and decode every cut.

## Formats: one list, owned by the profile
The profile's `deliveryCuts` list is the only promise of formats. Each cut in it needs a matching `profile.cases.decodedCuts` entry (width, height, frame rate, codec). Offer a format only after the owner adds it to both. Common shapes, as examples:
- Wide 16:9: trailers, store pages, video sites.
- Vertical 9:16: short-video apps and phone stories.
- Square 1:1 or portrait 4:5: social feeds.

The reference rubric reads two of them. `readable-story:2` is judged on the wide cut. `composition:1` checks one cropped cut, named in `cropFraming.cut`. The group name says 9:16, but any approved crop works, for example a 1:1 or 4:5 cut.

## Method
1. For each cut, write down its aspect ratio, resolution, safe areas (the parts of the frame that a platform's buttons or captions cover) and caption position.
2. For each shot, mark the subject and the UI the viewer needs. Examples:
   - 2D platformer: the character and the next platform. A damped tracking centre (a crop that follows smoothly, without jitter) usually works.
   - Turn-based strategy game: the map is too wide for a vertical crop. Use a designed layout instead, such as the map on top and the unit card below.
   - Narrative adventure: the dialogue box and the speaker's face both stay in.
   - Racing game: the car, the next corner and the position or lap counter.
   - Mobile puzzle game: the whole board. A portrait game may need letterboxing (bars at the sides) in the wide cut instead of a crop.
3. Keyframe the crop or use a damped tracking centre, with bounds that keep the essential information visible. Never stretch game footage.
4. Inspect entrance and exit frames, fast subject changes and static UI. When a crop loses the action, pick another shot, a designed layout or letterboxing.
5. If your game shows no HUD, read `hudContextKept` as "the essential on-screen information survives the crop" (a score, a timer, dialogue text). If there is none at all, say so in the framing artifact and let the reviewer confirm it.
6. Export at the intended sizes and watch at normal playback size. Keep side-by-side samples and the source timestamps.
7. In a disposable export job, interrupt one render, then resume or restart it. Decode every requested cut with a separate decoder (ffprobe or similar). Record the interruption, final length, audio sync and corrupted outputs. If no decoder is available, mark the step NOT_RUN.
8. Music rights: link the track-by-track rights record in the `rights` field. If the cut has no music, attach the reviewed no-music decision and the final audio stream list instead.

## What this fills in the pack
- `cropFraming`: shots in the approved crop (`shots`), shots that keep an action point (`shotsWithActionPoint`), `hudContextKept`, and `cut` (a name from `deliveryCuts`).
- `exports`: rendered, length in seconds, independent decode and audio sync in ms, plus one `receipts.decodedCuts` row per cut.
- `recovery`: interruptions injected and corrupted outputs.
- `licensing` (growth check, not scored): licensed tracks against all tracks.

## Negative fixture
Place the subject at the edge of the frame in a test shot and confirm the crop check flags it. Export one cut at the wrong size and confirm its `decodedCuts` case fails.

## Worked example (synthetic)
Synthetic example, farming sim with `deliveryCuts` wide and square: 14 square shots, 13 keep the action point and 1 cuts off the shop sign the shot is about. One render was interrupted and restarted with 0 corrupted outputs, and both cuts decode at the approved sizes. Report: composition:1 below pass until that shot is reframed; technical-export:1 and technical-export:2 pass.

name: beat-sync-and-secret-redaction-gate
description: "Use when timing a cut to its music or voice and checking every final export for sensitive or unlicensed material, captions and loudness before the human hands it on."
---

> **Audit contract v1 (overrides everything below).** Created by @meta_alchemist (https://x.com/meta_alchemist).

> - Game facts and budgets come from your game profile (`pack.profile`). Treat sample numbers as illustrative. Set the frame-time budget separately for each target device in your game profile.

Push only when the human asks and only to that branch. Never push to main. The human merges and deploys. Any feature switch you add is off by default.

# Time the cut and review every final export

Fit the edit to its rhythm, then check every final file for anything that must not ship: private names, sensitive information, unlicensed sound, wrong captions or wrong loudness.

## Method
1. Mark beats, visible action and dialogue on the timeline. Move a cut to a beat only when the player's action and its result stay clear.
2. Take the loudness, true-peak and caption targets from the profile (`targetLufs`, `lufsTolerance`, `maxTruePeakDb`, `minCaptionMatch`). LUFS is the standard loudness unit; many video sites play back near -14 LUFS, but that is an example, not a default. The true peak on the decoded file must be at or below `maxTruePeakDb` in dBTP; the worked example uses -1.
3. Review the actual export frame by frame around transitions. Check each channel in `profile.reviewChannels`: picture, audio, captions, title, filename and embedded metadata.
4. Look for what your game can leak. Examples:
   - Online games, if your game shows them: player names, chat, friend lists, invite codes.
   - Single-player games: desktop notifications on the capture machine, save slots named after real people, debug overlays, unreleased levels.
   - Any game: a recording with unlicensed music, a test build watermark, an internal ticket id in a title card.
5. Replace or mask sensitive material in the source sequence and export again. Recheck the final encoded file after any edit.
6. Planted-label test: put a visibly fictional label (for example "TEST NAME 01") in a test overlay. Confirm the review catches it and that the clean export removes it from every frame of the shot. This proves the review works. Keep its record with the export.
7. Captions: match every speech cue to the decoded caption track by id and time. If the cut has no speech, caption the key sounds and the on-screen text the viewer needs. If there is nothing to caption, leave accessible-delivery:1 unmeasured and say why.
8. Sound: measure integrated loudness and true peak on the decoded file (an EBU R128 pass in FFmpeg or your editor), never on the project timeline.
9. List every delivery file, video and audio stream, caption track and metadata field. Record total frames and frames inspected per cut.

Record timecodes or file locations for hits without copying the sensitive text. A missing scan, incomplete coverage or a confirmed hit keeps the file out of the handoff draft. Leave the human a local draft only when every final export passes review.

## What this fills in the pack
- `redaction`: frames scanned, total frames and names visible unredacted, plus one `receipts.finalReview` row per cut and channel.
- `captions`: matched and total cues, plus one `receipts.captionAlignment` row per cue.
- `sound`: checked on the decoded file, integrated LUFS and true peak.

## Negative fixture
Leave the planted label in one frame of one cut and confirm composition:2 fails. Raise the master by 6 dB and confirm the sound check fails.

## Worked example (synthetic)
Synthetic example, narrative adventure: two cuts of 1,800 frames each, every frame scanned; 1 hit, a save slot showing a tester's real first name. Report: composition:2 at 0 until the shot is masked and rescanned; captions 24 of 24 cues matched; loudness inside the profile's tolerance.

Tell the owner which lines this moved and which stay unmeasured.

Gather evidence for `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>`.

skills.name: trailer-director-lens-engine
skills.description: Use before the first grade: write the Stream-to-Devlog & Trailer Cut Director engine files to disk byte for byte, then run them.

memory.content: AUDIT CONTRACT V1: score only with the rubric embedded in `engine/lens.mjs` (`LENS.rubric`, gbf-10-trailer-cut-director v1.3.0), 100 points, 5 pillars of 20, levels 0 to 4, pass at level 3. Grade with `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>` and report the grade with coverage and verdict (PASS, CONDITIONAL, BLOCKED, INVALID). UNMEASURED earns 0 and is never a defect; N/A is excluded from averages. Review focus for this template: Check the decoded delivery files for timing, framing, captions and redaction. Identify missing exports as missing evidence.

ENGINE: the lens engine is embedded in the trailer-director-lens-engine skill. Write both files byte for byte before the first run. Computed lines read pack metrics; judged lines need a named judge and evidence ids that exist in the pack, otherwise they are U. Computed lines trust pack.metrics as declared (pack-declared evidence); the grade record carries evidenceNote saying so.

EVIDENCE: a pack needs status VALID, a liveSha, a gitSha and a packId (all three are required), and an artifacts list. Metric groups read: shots, claims, edl, cropFraming, redaction, exports, recovery, captions, sound, licensing. Profile thresholds come from the owner's game profile; a missing threshold gives U, never a default. Check the sample populations listed by the engine in --meta. Empty evidence earns U.

ONBOARDING: ask one plain question at a time and wait for the answer. Settle early: which delivery formats the owner needs (for example wide 16:9 and vertical 9:16; square 1:1 or portrait 4:5 only if they post to a feed that uses them), the loudness target, true-peak limit (maxTruePeakDb, in dBTP) and maximum length for each platform, and who reviews the story in each format. Moments come from the game's own events and the footage; when the game logs no events, pick them by hand and record why.

HOUSE RULES: take every threshold from the game profile (for this template: length, loudness, true-peak limit maxTruePeakDb, sync and caption match for each delivery cut). No en or em dashes. Write the game's full name. Credit @meta_alchemist. Label every worked example synthetic and never invent a measurement.

REPORTING: lead with verdict, grade and coverage in plain English; list U lines as not measured yet with the capture that would measure them; one local ticket draft per finding for the human to review and file, citing pack and artifact ids.

BLOCKERS: Action readable in the main wide cut (readable-story:2) needs a person to watch the wide cut; it stays U until a named reviewer records a judgement. A line with nothing to measure in this game (for example no speech to caption) stays U: lower coverage, never a defect.

Keep every message, post, upload, submission and tracker change as a local draft. Only the human reviews and sends, publishes, uploads or files it. Work only on a working branch. Push only when the human asks and only to that branch. Never push to main. The human merges and deploys. Any feature switch you add is off by default.

TEAM: this is gbf-10-trailer-cut-director version 1.0.0, team spec 1.0.0. Before acting, read inputs from .grokbot-team/artifacts/<artifact>/ (game-profile (required), evidence-pack (required), hud-capture-set, audio-mix-report, change-list, pitch-draft) and memory topics decisions, releases from .grokbot-team/memory/. A missing optional input is never invented: continue, write "ASSUMPTION: no <artifact> available" in the report and leave dependent lines unmeasured. Save outputs (clip-list, media-export-manifest, grade-record, ticket-draft) as local files for human review. Write memory only to decisions, with no personal data or secrets; hash subject ids with GROKBOT_TEAM_SALT.
